newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Share Trust launches passive fund to track NZSE-40.
newsitem.headline: Share Trust launches passive fund to track NZSE-40.

text.p: The New Zealand Share Index Trust Ltd, a company formed in association with sharebroker Frater Williams and Co., on Wednesday launched a passive fund tracking the NZSE-40 Capital Index.
The Trust said it would operate the NZ Top 40 Fund and the New Zealand Guardian Trust Limited would act as trustee and custodian of all fund assets.

Trust director Peter Mellor said he expected strong interest in the fund. "For the first time the NZSE-40 -- the barometer of the New Zealand sharemarket -- will be replicated by a passive fund," he said in a statement.
The NZ Top 40 Fund would use the NZSE-40 index as its valuation tool and the value of units would be approximately one l,000th of the NZSE-40 index.
"For example, if the NZSE-40 index is (at) 2,240, the unit value will be NZ$2.24," Mellor said.
He said investors could choose lump sum payments (minimum $500), monthly investments (minimum $100), or a combination of both. Investors could also choose to reinvest dividend income six-montly.
Mellor said the fund was the broadest representation of the New Zealand sharemarket, covering 92.8 percent of the total market compared with the next largest, TeNZ, at 67.2 percent.
The fund had an annual management fee of 0.2 per cent and would be available to investors from May 5.
